title: Inference size-reduction sprint journal
notes:
Sprint goal: identify a reproducible strategy to reduce GPU memory and per-token cost for customer X’s retrieval-augmented classification service while preserving >= 95% task accuracy compared to baseline floating-point model. Rapid experiments + simple deployable knobs (no full retrain).

Context and constraints:
- Customer workload: short queries (avg 55 tokens), dense retrieval returns 3 passages (avg 250 tokens each). End-to-end latency SLO: 250ms P95 for single-query interactive flow. Throughput target for Dedicated: 3500 qps sustained across table of users.
- Privacy: customer prefers Dedicated or Private. No model fine-tuning allowed on customer data; only post-training compression and prompt engineering.
- Baseline model: open-llm-13b (fp16) used in hosted test env. Baseline metrics measured on A100-40GB: mem 34GB, latency 180ms P95 per request (with prefix caching), cost/unit X.

Quick wins tried in sprint (ordered by implementation effort):
1) Layer-wise quantization with minimal calibration (GPTQ-lite): int8 for matmuls + fp16 for outliers. Deployment effort: ~2 dev-days to add GPTQ-lite artifact and validation harness.
   - Result: model size -28%, working memory -26%, P95 latency down 8ms, accuracy delta -0.9% (macro F1). Observed scattered hallucination on long numeric passages (edge case).
   - Tradeoff note: some ops still require fp16, but throughput improved because less memory pressure allowed larger effective batch.

2) KV cache sharding + per-request prefix trimming: trim retrieval context to top-2 paragraphs for generation-only stage; stream retrieval separately.
   - Result: avg tokens per call dropped 18%, latency P95 improved 12ms, end-to-end pipeline simpler. Accuracy impact: -0.5%.
   - Implementation: routing change + small prompt template edit.

3) Mixed precision with dynamic outlier clipping (Apex-like): enable fp16 with occasional fp32 fallback for norm ops.
   - Result: negligible size change, latency slightly better for long sequences, accuracy roughly identical. Risk: numerical instability on some aggressive quant configs.

4) Embedding caching for hot queries (edge-case): small LRU of 10k keys in memcached to avoid re-embedding retrieval candidates.
   - Result: reduced CPU embedding cost but little effect on token-inference cost.

Controlled experiments (longer-running):
- 4-bit quant (PTQ + per-channel scaling) using manufacturer kernel (custom CUDA int4): model size -53%, working memory -47%, but P95 latency increased 20ms on A100 due to kernel overhead; accuracy drop -2.8%.
  - Conclusion: int4 beneficial for throughput-bounded batched workloads but hurts single-request latency on our current serving kernel. Potentially better on newer hardware (H100 or custom int4 kernels) — test queued.

- Hybrid routing: keep fp16 primary, route 1% of traffic to fp32 variant for rare edge inputs (detector by perplexity and prompt length). This served well as safety net; produced negligible cost uplift (~+1.3%).

Key metrics summary (representative):
- Baseline fp16: size 13.2GB, mem 34GB, P95 latency 180ms, macro F1 0.842
- GPTQ-lite int8: size 9.5GB, mem 25GB, P95 172ms, macro F1 0.833
- Int4 PTQ: size 6.1GB, mem 18GB, P95 200ms, macro F1 0.819
- Mixed-precision + trimming: size same as baseline, mem 28GB, P95 168ms, macro F1 0.837

Operational checklist for proposed POC rollout:
- Day 0: smoke test quantized artifact on staging with canonical eval set + adversarial numeric checks. Add sanity checks to console (token-level divergence thresholds).
- Day 2: Canary (1% traffic) in Dedicated pool with routing knob; monitor latency, error rate, quality metrics in Optimize dashboard.
- Day 5: Ramp to 20% if quality delta < 1% and latency within SLO.
- Day 10: Full rollout if sustained; otherwise rollback and run regression analysis on failing prompts.

Prompt and pipeline tuning notes (quick reference):
- Move costly instructions (e.g., "explain step-by-step") into an optional secondary call; primary call returns concise classification label with short rationale metadata.
- Normalize retrieval formatting: strip stopwords and non-UTF characters, re-rank passages by combined embedding+BM25 signal before sending to model.
- Use concise system instruction template with explicit output schema (JSON) to reduce token churn.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Kernel availability: test int4 kernels on H100 and on our Dedicated fleet; collect perf vs A100. (Owner: Diego)
- Regression root cause: for GPTQ-lite case, investigate numeric outliers causing hallucination in tables (ticket JIRA-ENG-9982). Add dedicated numeric-preserving quant path.
- Cost modeling: recompute per-10k requests cost with new batching assumptions and effective token reduction; update proposal for Dedicated sizing.
- Can we compress attention matrices with SVD-based low-rank approximation without retraining? Prototype ideas exist but require careful validation on accuracy.

Customer-facing proposal excerpt (to send in follow-up email):
"We propose a two-track approach: short-term (4 weeks) deployable compression + prompt rework to yield ~20–30% unit cost reduction with <1% accuracy loss; mid-term (2–3 months) hardware-aligned int4 deployment and routing heuristics for additional 30–50% reduction on throughput-heavy workloads. We will maintain a canary/policy fallback to ensure no customer-visible degradation."

Workshop notes (from 2025-01-28 session):
- Hands-on: built int8 patched artifact and observed memory drop live; customer team liked the deployment path.
- Risk discussion: regulatory team insisted on deterministic logs and ability to replay quantized inference for audits — we committed to adding quant artifact hashes to audit logs.
- Action items: Diego to run H100 kernel benchmarks; Priya to prepare regen prompt set for numeric edge cases; Liam to add traffic-sampling end-to-end traces to console.

Appendix: quick commands & artifacts used in experiments (for reproducibility)
- eval harness: repo/github link above (see PR 142), run with --seed 42 --calib-samples 2k
- GPTQ-lite conversion script: tools/gptq-lite/convert.sh --group-size 64
- Canary routing config example: routes/prod-dedicated.json (snippet in Confluence page)

Notes to self:
- Keep experiment notebooks short and attach CSVs to Confluence. Avoid burying raw logs in Drive.
- When presenting to customer, show both cost curves and representative failure cases side-by-side.

End of sprint journal. Next sync planned 2025-02-22.
summary: Sprint journal capturing experiments to reduce inference memory and per-token cost for a retrieval-augmented classification POC. Explored int8 GPTQ-lite, int4 PTQ, mixed precision, KV trimming, and prompt/pipeline edits. Includes rollout checklist, workshop notes, and follow-ups.
